title: USMNT Player Ratings vs. Haiti: Mauricio Pochettino’s Farewell Tour Off to Perfect Start
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas6:57 PM ESTChristian Pulisic (middle) stole the show on Saturday.   / Leonardo Fernandez/USSF/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team ignored the noise surrounding Mauricio Pochettino’s exit and produced a flawless performance to defeat Haiti 6–0 in the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals.

It took the USMNT just 10 minutes to evidence its superiority by capturing an early lead. Sebastian Berhalter floated a perfect set piece that Auston Trusty nicely tucked into the net with a volley after appearing unmarked at the far post.
The game remained up in the air for a while, but a nice move saw teenager Julian Hall tap in the USMNT’s second seven minutes after the restart. Then, the floodgates opened.

Christian Pulisic took over the game and bagged a brace in a matter of two minutes. He calmly dispatched a penalty he created, and one minute later, he struck again with a perfectly placed weak-footed shot from distance into the bottom corner. Weston McKennie added a fifth in the 68th minute with an emphatic header from a set piece.
After getting a goal disallowed, Folarin Balogun was a man on a mission and announced his return to the USMNT with a strong finish to add a sixth inside the final 10 minutes.

In the second to last game of his tenure, Pochettino’s men delivered a dominant performance that has essentially clinched their place in March’s Nations League finals. Now, Tuesday’s second leg can be all about the USMNT and Pochettino having the best goodbye possible.

The USMNT has a discovered gem in Julian Hall.  / JC Ruiz/Getty ImagesIn the first official match following the World Cup, regular starters such as Weston McKennie and Christian Pulisic reclaimed their spots in the starting XI after missing the most recent international window. Not Folarin Balogun, though, who now faces increased competition at center forward.

After scoring three goals in his first three games for the Stars and Stripes, 18-year-old striker Julian Hall led the line for the USMNT on Saturday ahead of Balogun. The decision raised some eyebrows, but Hall validated Pochettino’s decision as he made it four goals in five games to start his international career.

The Red Bull New York teenager produced yet another brilliant performance as he continues to take advantage of his opportunities. Beyond goals, Hall meshes brilliantly with those around him. He’s impossible to pin down, given he’s constantly making runs and offering himself as an outlet, always appearing as an option when other forwards and midfielders lift their heads up in the final third.

Hall’s intelligence has become abundantly clear during his early USMNT career. He has an understanding of the center forward position rarely seen at his age, which allows him to become almost a magnet for goalscoring opportunities.
Balogun is a proven asset at the international level, but as Hall continues to perform and develop, a very tasty battle to be the main man up front is brewing.
Pochettino deployed his strongest XI.  / Leonardo Fernandez/USSF/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Diego Kochen—7.5: Brilliant one-on-one save to maintain the lead early in the contest. VAR erased his lone error of the night, as he got caught in halfway in his attempt to win the ball outside of his penalty area, but it was an otherwise strong showing from the young goalkeeper.

RB: Alex Freeman—8.1: Underwhelming from the Villarreal man, as Haiti took advantage of his rather loose marking effort to create its best chances of the match. Often late in his defensive interventions.
CB: Chris Richards—7.3: Commanded the backline with tremendous confidence. After a hot start, he imposed his will on the physical Lenny Joseph.
CB: Auston Trusty—8.1: Lovely volley to give his side an early lead and handled his defensive duties flawlessly, constantly stifling the dangerous Wilson Isidor.

LB: Antonee Robinson—8.6: Took a blow to the face and got booked inside the first five minutes. Robinson settled and almost single-handedly dominated the left flank. He did so effectively and bagged an assist.
CM: Sebastian Berhalter—8.2: Comfortable on the ball, unbothered by Haiti’s weak pressing efforts. His excellent deliveries from set pieces remain an absolute weapon for the USMNT.
CM: Tyler Adams—7.6: Seemingly every rebound or second ball found its way to Adams. The USMNT captain dominated in midfield and was the main reason why his side overwhelmingly dominated possession.
